title: Lebesgue-null abnormal minimizing set for sub-Riemannian distances whose minimizing horizontal paths have Goh-rank at most 1
difficulty_reason: The quoted Agrachev-Lee Lipschitzness result applies only when no minimizing path carries a Goh-condition abnormal lift, so it says nothing when minimizing paths have Goh-rank exactly 1, and no existing subdifferential criterion decides a Lebesgue-null statement about the abnormal minimizing set. The author proves a one-dimensional almost-everywhere dichotomy between differentiability and being a limit of points where the function reaches local minima, with Denjoy-Young-Saks sharpening the second alternative into the middle Dini derivative being finite, and uses it to convert the Goh-rank-at-most-1 hypothesis into a Lipschitz support function from below along a hypersurface transverse to a minimizing path. The theorem then follows from a quantitative scheme the author builds step by step: density-point localization to a ball with a globally parametrized distribution; a preparatory perturbation proposition producing, for each nearby point, a control whose endpoint moves within a controlled distance and whose energy changes only by that distance; an explicit projected perturbation estimate bounding the pointed distance from below by the transported support function on the transverse curve; and a viscosity barrier max{-eps(s-a), eps(s-b)} closed by contradiction on the two sides of the transverse interval. The second-order local-openness index condition used at the bottom of the chain is proved in an appendix as a refinement of the cited book theorem rather than quoted. This apparatus, not the corollary cases, is what turns the new hypothesis into the null-set conclusion.
